question.text: Fund PPI, a Category III AIF, subscribes to Pre-IPO shares of Company ABC at INR 120/share before the IPO at INR 130/share. Under the SEBI (ICDR) Regulations, 2018, the Pre-IPO shares held by institutional investors including AIFs are subject to:

answer.text: No lock-in since AIFs are exempt institutional investors
A 3-year lock-in from the date of Pre-IPO allotment, regardless of IPO timing
A lock-in period from the date of listing of the shares through the IPO
Lock-in only if the AIF receives more than 10% of the IPO size

explanation.text: **The Logic:** Per Ch 11.2.4.3 (Pre-IPO Strategy) and SEBI (ICDR) Regulations 2018, institutional investors including AIFs subscribing to Pre-IPO shares or QIP are subject to a lock-in period from the date of listing of such shares through the IPO. The lock-in clock starts on listing, not on Pre-IPO allotment. **The Trap:** AIFs are NOT exempt — this is a common misconception with retail carve-outs. Option C gets the trigger date wrong (it's listing, not allotment). Option D invents a size threshold that doesn't exist in ICDR. **Cross-Exam Context:** XIX-A tests Pre-IPO as a product. XIX-C tests the Manager's compliance obligation — lock-in sits on the AIF's books and must be disclosed in PPM liquidity section. **Manager's Pro-Tip:** Bake the Pre-IPO lock-in into your NAV liquidity schedule BEFORE subscribing. LPs who assume they can exit at IPO-listing day will sour on the fund if they learn of lock-in only at the listing date.
